Trump International Airport in West Palm Beach After Thunderstorm Delays
 Why It Matters Short weather ground stops at a single destination airport can hold up traffic from several upstream regions at once, a recurring constraint on Florida's busy private and charter flying.
 Nov 18 Disclaimer WSBT Save The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted a ground stop for flights headed to President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT) in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Wednesday afternoon. The ground stop followed flight delays caused by thunderstorms. According to the FAA, it began at 1:51 p.m. CBS12 News reported from the airport that there were no more delays as of 4:10 p.m. 
 The restriction applied to flights departing from three FAA air traffic control regions: Atlanta, Jacksonville and Miami . Those regions cover multiple airports, so flights bound for West Palm Beach from several locations were affected.
